stories.title: US will strike Iran if Tehran responds to sanctions with military escalation — secretary
stories.summary: WASHINGTON, August 24. The United States will respond rapidly to any Iranian attack if the Islamic Republic reacts to Washington’s promised "unprecedented sanctions" with military escalation, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote in an article for the Financial Times (FT). Bessent said that US President Donald Trump would respond swiftly and decisively if Iran took military action against US troops or its neighbors in the Persian Gulf as the regime’s power weakened along with its economy. He also said that the US goal at this stage is to completely isolate Iran economically. Earlier, Bessent wrote on his X page that the US plans to launch a "financial offensive" against Iran on Monday. Trump had previously announced the start of an "economic warfare and isolation" against Iran on an unprecedented scale. The US president also warned that countries whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government agencies support Tehran would face severe economic consequences from the United States. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said in response that the US sanctions policy toward Iran is economic terrorism and a crime against humanity. The ministry added that the US administration, the sanctions planners and their enforcers must face appropriate punishment.

stories.title: Seville, Jefferson-Wooden roar to 100m wins at Silesia Diamond League
stories.summary: Brazil’s Alison Dos Santos beats world record holder Karsten Warholm in a thrilling 400m hurdles final at the meet. World 100m champions Oblique Seville and Melissa Jefferson-Wooden roared to victories at the Silesia Diamond League as Armand ‘Mondo’ Duplantis wrapped up another dominant pole vault display. World champion Seville of Jamaica posted a time of 9.83 seconds for a meet record, as Americans Kenny Bednarek (9.87) and Christian Coleman (9.93) completed the podium. The women’s blue riband event was won by their teammate Jefferson-Wooden in the season’s first head-to-head over 100m with Olympic champion Julien Alfred, in a season’s best of 10.78 seconds. Olympic silver medallist Sha’Carri Richardson trailed in third at 10.96. Duplantis had an uncharacteristic three failures in the pole vault before claiming victory at 6.20m, ahead of Norway’s Sondre Guttormsen, who took silver at 6.00m, while Greek rival Emmanouil Karalis bagged bronze at the same height. Brazil’s Alison Dos Santos delivered another standout performance as he held off world record holder Karsten Warholm in a thrilling 400m hurdles to win in 46.43 seconds, the sixth-fastest time ever run. The world-leading time smashed the meet record of 46.82 seconds set by Warholm last year. “I expected a fast race, the lineup was amazing — everybody was here,” said Dos Santos. “I knew that to win here I had to give my best.” Warholm’s teammate Jakob Ingebrigtsen, fresh from winning European 5,000m gold, made his first Diamond League appearance in a 1,500m race in two years. Ingebrigtsen clung on to finish fourth in a race won by American Ethan Strand in 3:30.77, ahead of Kenya’s Phanuel Kipkosegi Koech and Olympic champion Cole Hocker of the US.

stories.title: Banking veteran Li Yun fills senior Shenzhen posts in countdown to Apec
stories.summary: A banking veteran has been appointed the new deputy Communist Party secretary and acting mayor of the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen, just months before the city is scheduled to host a series of Apec meetings. The positions have been filled by Li Yun, who spent more than two decades working in financial institutions and has been the vice-governor of Guangdong province since March last year.
